source.title: Faithful and Stable Neuron Explanations for Trustworthy Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Ge Yan; Tuomas Oikarinen;  Tsui-Wei;  Weng

record.tranche_reason: The paper analyzes neuron-explanation faithfulness using generalization bounds and experiments on similarity metrics and probing datasets. This bears conceptually on whether explanations generalize beyond the data used to identify them, but it does not use the original audit procedure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports synthetic and vision-model results on similarity-metric generalization and explanation stability. It does not report neuron-pole job shares, language-model audits, attribution graphs, or automated explanation scores on new text. No results cited from other work are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper gives a theoretical and simulated analysis of how faithful and stable neuron-identification similarity scores are with respect to probing-set size, metric and concept frequency. It also gives bootstrap stability results for NetDissect and CLIP-Dissect on vision backbones. It reports no share of neurons with one main job, no language-model audit, no attribution graphs and no rate of explanations failing to predict held-out activations. The synthetic runs simulate metric estimators, not neurons. The one real-data probing-size result (Fig. 9) is a few qualitative examples. Stability scores are a related but different construct. So no version is tested; findings go to fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors frame neuron identification as inverse learning and derive generalization bounds for faithfulness. They also propose a bootstrap ensemble (BE) giving concept prediction sets with coverage guarantees, validated on synthetic data and vision models.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops theoretical generalization and bootstrap-stability analyses for vision-model neuron-identification methods; it does not reproduce the original neuron-pole audit or score language-model explanations on new text.
record.method_sensitivity: Metric convergence varies with concept frequency: for the rare-concept simulation, AUROC and recall perform much worse than precision and IoU. The paper also reports that explanation accuracy improves with larger probing datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Bootstrap stability of identified concepts varies by method and backbone. NetDissect top-1 frequency is 91.3% on ViT-B/16 vs 27.8% on ConvNeXt-Base; CLIP-Dissect ranges 51.2–66.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron-explanation stability across probing resamples depends on the identification method and model backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: Similarity-metric estimates converge at about O(1/sqrt(n)) in probing-set size. AUROC and recall converge poorly for rare concepts. Real-data examples suggest larger probing sets give more accurate concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Faithfulness of neuron explanations depends on probing-set size, concept frequency and similarity metric.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2025 Workshop: Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop at NeurIPS 2025
record.problems: The real-model experiments are on vision models, not language models. The probing-size comparison is qualitative, and the paper does not report a rate of explanation failures on held-out activations. Its limitations section notes that the generalization bound does not use relations among concepts and that bootstrap ensembles add computational overhead.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant result rows omitted. Profiling runtime and memory overhead are not measures of neuron-explanation faithfulness, job shares, or stability outcomes.

untested.parts: Job shares across language models, dense and MoE, and across scale.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car reinterpretation and recursive generalization.
Interpretable-neuron share as a function of architecture and tools.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without replacement models.
Whether explanations fitting activating examples fail to predict where a neuron fires; the paper only bounds metric estimation error in theory and simulation.
Simulation-based scoring of explanations on new text and the share of neurons with good scores.

record.verdict_notes: The study covers vision models only (ResNet-50, ViT-B/16, ConvNeXt-Base) and cites neither original source. The reader's V6 limits_scope label was removed: r6 is qualitative and does not measure held-out firing prediction.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B pole shares and the proportions with one job, two related jobs, or no known job.
Cross-model and scale comparisons of neuron-job shares, including dense and mixture-of-experts language models.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car interpretation, pose, and recursive generalization.
Architecture/tool effects on the proportion of interpretable neurons and the stated InceptionV1-sized model estimates.
Attribution graphs constructed from a large model's own neurons and reconstruction error from replacement models.

The paper studies faithfulness/generalization across probing datasets, but does not directly test explanations generated from activating examples against a separately specified set of firing locations in a language model.
Automated explanation scores from simulated activations on new text and the share of neurons achieving good scores.

rows.subject: synthetic data
rows.operation_detail: Compared similarity-metric estimation errors across probing-dataset sizes in the regular-concept simulation.
rows.measure: 95% quantile of similarity error as sample count changes
rows.value: Accuracy converges fastest; IoU, recall and precision are similar; AUROC converges faster than those three.
rows.uncertainty: 95% quantile of error; no other uncertainty stated
rows.note: Reports convergence of metric estimates, not an observed rate of explanations that fail on held-out activations.
rows.check: Synthetic metric-estimator convergence, with no neurons or explanations; it does not measure V6's held-out firing prediction.

rows.subject: synthetic data
rows.operation_detail: Compared similarity-metric estimation errors across probing-dataset sizes in the rare-concept simulation.
rows.measure: 95% quantile of similarity error as sample count changes
rows.value: Accuracy converges fastest; AUROC and recall perform much worse than precision and IoU.
rows.uncertainty: 95% quantile of error; no other uncertainty stated
rows.note: Shows metric- and concept-frequency-dependent estimation behavior, not a direct held-out firing test of generated explanations.
rows.check: Synthetic rare-concept metric convergence; not a measure of explanations failing on new inputs.

rows.subject: synthetic data
rows.operation_detail: Simulated the gap between the best candidate concept and the concept selected from probing data.
rows.value: All curves have a similar slope to O(1/√n); accuracy has the fastest convergence constant and AUROC the second fastest.
rows.uncertainty: 95% quantile used to approximate the bound at success probability 95%
rows.note: The simulated gap concerns concept selection under the stated metric; it is not a direct rate of explanation failures on new activations.
rows.check: Simulated selection gap validating Thm 3.1 on synthetic probability matrices; no real neuron explanations.

rows.subject: synthetic data
rows.operation_detail: Measured convergence of continuous-representation similarity metrics on synthetic data.
rows.measure: 95% quantile of metric error versus sample count
rows.value: All metrics show asymptotic O(1/√N) convergence.
rows.note: Metric convergence is measured; the result does not report how often an explanation fits examples but fails to predict activations.
rows.check: Synthetic Gaussian convergence of continuous metrics; not a V6 measure.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Measured similarity-metric convergence for final-layer neurons using ImageNet validation data and predicted class labels as concepts.
rows.measure: 95% quantile of metric error versus sample count
rows.value: AUROC performs significantly better with more samples; most metrics show asymptotic O(1/√N) convergence.
rows.note: This measures metric convergence for vision-model neurons, not the frequency of explanations that fail to predict firing on held-out examples.
rows.check: Estimator convergence for ResNet-50 final-layer neurons against their own class labels; no explanation is tested for held-out prediction.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Compared CLIP-Dissect explanations for layer 4 neurons using different probing-dataset sizes.
rows.measure: Qualitative accuracy of the captured concept as probing data increases
rows.value: The authors state that with more probing data, the captured concept describes the neurons more accurately.
rows.note: Qualitative vision-model result; the paper does not give a rate of held-out explanation failures.
rows.check: Qualitative examples only (Fig. 9), with no held-out activation-prediction score. 'Partial' is not readable from this.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Applied bootstrap resampling to compare explanation outcomes from two neuron-identification methods.
rows.measure: Stability and concreteness of identified concepts across bootstrap samples
rows.value: NetDissect is described as more stable and as tending to identify concrete concepts.
rows.note: Stability/concreteness does not measure the claim versions' neuron-job shares or held-out prediction performance.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Applied bootstrap resampling to compare explanation outcomes from two neuron-identification methods.
rows.measure: Stability and diversity of identified concepts across bootstrap samples
rows.value: CLIP-Dissect is described as producing more diverse and more abstract concepts; it sometimes captures concepts missed by NetDissect.
rows.note: Stability/diversity is not one of the claim versions' specified measures.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CLIP-Dissect on ResNet-50 layer 4 with ImageNet validation probing sets of 100, 1000, 10000, and 50000 examples
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports that concepts describe neurons more accurately with more probing data, indicating that explanation faithfulness depends on probing-set size; this is qualitative and does not quantify held-out failure rates (r6).
